questions.question: What is the distribution of a random variable $X$?
options: The sample space before any random variable is defined, rather than the distribution
The largest value that $X$ can take
The probability measure on $\mathbb R$ assigning $P(X\in B)$ to suitable sets $B$
The single most likely value of $X$
questions.explanation: The distribution of $X$ is the probability measure on $\mathbb R$ that assigns each suitable set $B$ the probability $P(X\in B)$.
questions.source_support: The definition assigns to each suitable set $B$ the probability $P(X\in B)$.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
option_explanations: The sample space is where outcomes live before defining $X$; it is not the distribution of $X$.
The largest value is the maximum of the support, not the whole distribution.
The single most likely value is the mode, not the whole distribution.
